I'm working on integrating patch awareness into the dependency resolution phase of a package manager.

*   ResolveDependencyTreeOptions must include a new field `patched_dependencies: Option<Arc<PatchGroupRecord>>`. All existing call sites that construct this struct must be updated to supply the field (set to `None` when no patching is required).

*   ResolveImporterOptions must include a new field `patched_dependencies: Option<Arc<PatchGroupRecord>>`. This field is forwarded to the inner ResolveDependencyTreeOptions used by the orchestrator.

*   ResolvedTree must include an `applied_patches` field (a set of strings, e.g. HashSet<String>) that records which patch keys were successfully matched during resolution. It must support `contains` and `is_empty` operations.

*   ResolveDependencyTreeError must have a PatchKeyConflict variant. This variant is returned by resolve_dependency_tree when two or more range-based patch entries in patched_dependencies both satisfy the resolved version of the same package.

*   When patched_dependencies contains an exact-version entry matching a resolved package's name and version, resolve_dependency_tree must append `(patch_hash=<hash>)` to the package ID (e.g. `foo@1.0.0` becomes `foo@1.0.0(patch_hash=abc123)`) and add the patch key (e.g. `foo@1.0.0`) to ResolvedTree.applied_patches.

*   When patched_dependencies contains a range entry whose version range satisfies the resolved package's version (via semver satisfies), resolve_dependency_tree must append `(patch_hash=<hash>)` to the package ID and add the configured range key (e.g. `foo@^1.0.0`) to ResolvedTree.applied_patches.

*   When two or more range-based patch entries in patched_dependencies all satisfy the resolved version of a package, resolve_dependency_tree must return Err(ResolveDependencyTreeError::PatchKeyConflict(_)) rather than silently picking one patch.

*   When patched_dependencies is Some but no entry matches any resolved package (e.g. the patch is for a different package name or an unresolved version), all package IDs must remain unchanged and ResolvedTree.applied_patches must be empty.

*   After resolve_dependency_tree produces a ResolvedTree with patched package IDs, calling resolve_peers on that tree must propagate the full patched IDs (including the `(patch_hash=...)` suffix) to the DepPath values in direct_dependencies_by_alias.

*   The pacquet_patching crate must publicly export ExtendedPatchInfo, PatchGroup, PatchGroupRangeItem, and PatchGroupRecord so that callers can construct patched_dependencies values. PatchGroup must derive Default.

1	//! Port of pnpm's
2	//! [`resolveRootDependencies`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/097983fbca/installing/deps-resolver/src/resolveDependencies.ts#L327-L437)
3	//! — the multi-pass loop that hoists missing peers into the importer's
4	//! direct deps until no required peer is missing and no optional peer
5	//! is satisfiable from the in-flight preferred-versions map.
6	//!
7	//! Two nested fixed-point loops:
8	//!
9	//! 1. **Inner / required pass.** Run [`fn@crate::resolve_peers`] over the
10	//!    growing tree, collect peers that are required (not optional) and
11	//!    not already direct deps, pick a specifier per peer via
12	//!    [`fn@crate::hoist_peers`], and extend the tree with those picks.
13	//!    Repeat until the picker proposes nothing new.
14	//! 2. **Outer / optional pass.** Aggregate the optional missing peers
15	//!    seen across the inner-loop iterations, ask
16	//!    [`fn@crate::get_hoistable_optional_peers`] which of them have a
17	//!    preferred version already in scope, and extend the tree with
18	//!    those. Re-enter the inner loop if any landed.
19	//!
20	//! Single-importer slice; multi-importer support waits on pacquet's

5	//! depth-first, propagating a [`ParentRefs`] map of available parents

9	//! `direct → DepPath` map the install layer consumes.

11	//! **Scope of this port.** The slice landing here covers the
12	//! correctness surface — peer matching, depPath construction with
13	//! per-occurrence variation, missing / bad peer issue collection,
14	//! transitive-peer propagation, and the basic cycle break. Upstream
15	//! also runs three optimisations on top of the algorithm that pacquet
16	//! does **not** port yet:
17	//!
18	//! - **`peersCache`** — caches resolved peer combinations keyed by
19	//!   `pkgIdWithPatchHash` so a repeat visit short-circuits the walk.
20	//!   Pacquet always recomputes; correctness is unaffected.
21	//! - **`purePkgs` fast path** — a pure package (no resolved / missing
22	//!   peers) gets its depPath equal to its `pkgIdWithPatchHash` without
23	//!   recursing. The general path produces the same answer, just one
24	//!   walk later.
25	//! - **`graph-cycles`-driven async deferment** — upstream's
26	//!   `pathsByNodeIdPromises` lets a cyclic peer pick a `name@version`
27	//!   peer-id once `analyzeGraph` confirms the cycle. Pacquet performs
28	//!   a synchronous post-order traversal with an `in_progress` set; a
29	//!   re-entry on the same `NodeId` falls back to `name@version` as
30	//!   the peer-id, which is what upstream's cycle resolution converges

48	/// Pull `(name, version)` out of a `ResolveResult` the peer-resolution
49	/// stage can hash and compare on.
50	///
51	/// The npm-registry resolver always fills [`ResolveResult::name_ver`],
52	/// so the fast path lifts it straight out. The git / tarball / local
53	/// resolvers leave it `None` (their canonical name lives in the
54	/// fetched manifest, which the resolver doesn't read at resolve
55	/// time); for those, fall back to `(alias, id-as-string)`. The peer
56	/// graph machinery only ever looks the name up in
57	/// [`ResolvedTree::all_peer_dep_names`] — a set that comes from
58	/// upstream's `parsePeerDependencies` over npm-shaped packages — so
59	/// the fallback's "name" will simply miss every lookup, naturally
60	/// short-circuiting peer propagation for non-npm packages without
61	/// panicking on `name_ver = None`.
62	fn pkg_name_version(result: &ResolveResult) -> (String, String) {
63	    if let Some(name_ver) = result.name_ver.as_ref() {
64	        return (name_ver.name.to_string(), name_ver.suffix.to_string());
65	    }
66	    let fallback_name = result.alias.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| result.id.as_str().to_string());
67	    (fallback_name, result.id.as_str().to_string())
68	}

1	//! Port of pnpm's
2	//! [`@pnpm/installing.deps-resolver`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/097983fbca/installing/deps-resolver/src/index.ts).
3	//!
4	//! The public entry point for an install pass is
5	//! [`fn@resolve_importer`]: it owns three lower-level passes and the
6	//! `autoInstallPeers` hoist loop that ties them together.
7	//!
8	//! 1. **Tree pass** ([`fn@resolve_dependency_tree`]). Walks a project
9	//!    manifest's direct dependencies through a
10	//!    [`Resolver`](pacquet_resolving_resolver_base::Resolver) chain
11	//!    and recurses on every resolved package's own manifest
12	//!    dependencies. Produces:
13	//!
14	//!    - [`ResolvedTree::packages`] — flat dedup map keyed by
15	//!      `pkgIdWithPatchHash`, mirroring upstream's `resolvedPkgsById`.
16	//!    - [`ResolvedTree::dependencies_tree`] — per-occurrence tree
17	//!      keyed by [`NodeId`], mirroring upstream's `dependenciesTree`.
18	//!    - [`ResolvedTree::all_peer_dep_names`] — names every visited
19	//!      package declares as a peer, used by the peer pass as the
20	//!      `parentPkgs` filter.
21	//!
22	//!    Peer dependencies are **not** walked as regular edges during the
23	//!    tree pass. They are recorded on [`ResolvedPackage::peer_dependencies`]
24	//!    and consumed by the peer pass.
25	//!
26	//! 2. **Peer pass** ([`fn@resolve_peers`]). Walks the tree, matches each
27	//!    package's peer requirements against the parent chain, and
28	//!    produces [`DependenciesGraph`] — keyed by `DepPath` (one entry per
29	//!    `(pkgIdWithPatchHash, peer-suffix)` combination) and the entry
30	//!    point for the install layer.
31	//!
32	//! 3. **Hoist loop** ([`fn@resolve_importer`]). Runs passes 1–2,
33	//!    aggregates missing required and optional peers via
34	//!    [`fn@hoist_peers`] / [`fn@get_hoistable_optional_peers`], extends
35	//!    the tree with hoisted picks via
36	//!    [`extend_tree`], and re-runs the peer pass
37	//!    until both pass-1 and pass-2 reach a fixed point. Mirrors
38	//!    upstream's
39	//!    [`resolveRootDependencies`](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/blob/097983fbca/installing/deps-resolver/src/resolveDependencies.ts#L327-L437).
40	//!
41	//! This is intentionally a thin slice of upstream:
42	//!
43	//! - **Single importer.** Pacquet's install doesn't expose workspaces
44	//!   to the resolver yet; the entry point takes one manifest at a
45	//!   time.
46	//! - **No catalog / hook / lockfile-pinned-version bias.** The
47	//!   resolver is fed each child's manifest range verbatim. Lockfile-
48	//!   seeded preferred versions arrive via the orchestrator's
49	//!   `all_preferred_versions` option — callers pre-seed with the
50	//!   `pacquet-lockfile-preferred-versions` crate.

I integrated patch awareness into the dependency-resolution phase. All changes are in source files (the production call site plus the two in-crate unit-test modules that construct the options structs — neither lives in a `tests/` directory).

- Added `applied_patches: HashSet<String>` to `ResolvedTree`. `ResolvedTree` already derives `Default`, so `HashSet` supports `.contains(&str)` / `.is_empty()` out of the box.

### `resolving-deps-resolver/src/resolve_dependency_tree.rs`
- Added `patched_dependencies: Option<Arc<PatchGroupRecord>>` to `ResolveDependencyTreeOptions`.
- Added `ResolveDependencyTreeError::PatchKeyConflict(PatchKeyConflictError)` (transparent diagnostic reusing the patching crate's existing error).
- Threaded `patched_dependencies` and a new `applied_patches: Mutex<HashSet<String>>` through `TreeCtx` (new `TreeCtx::new` signature; both `into_resolved_tree` and `snapshot` emit `applied_patches`).
